verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तस्मिन् बहुमृगेऽरण्ये अटमाना महारथाः। काम्यके भरतश्रेष्ठा विजह्रुस्ते यथाऽमराः॥१॥
verses.english: Viashampayana said : Those mighty car-warriors, the foremost of the Bharata race, wandering like immortals in the forest of Kamyaka abounding in many deer, were pleased.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षमाणा बहुविधान् वनोद्देशान् समन्ततः। यथर्तुकालरम्याश्च वनराजीः सपुष्पिताः॥२॥
verses.english: Beholding various wild tracts of country on all sides, the woodland decorated with the beautiful, blossming season flowers.
Those Indra-like Pandavas, fond of hunting and subdues of their enemies, lived there for some time wandering in that huge forest.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ते यौगपद्येन ययुः सर्वे चतुर्दिशम्। मृगयां पुरुषव्याघ्रा ब्राह्मणार्थे परन्तपाः॥४॥
verses.english: One day those men, those repressors of their enemies, wandered about on all sides, in search of game for feeding the Brahmanas who were with them, leaving Draupadi alone in the hermitage with the permission of Trinabindu the great ascetic of burning asceticism and their priest Dhaumya.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपदीमाश्रमे न्यस्य तृणबिन्दोरनुज्ञया। महर्षेर्दीप्ततपसो धौम्यस्य च पुरोधसः॥५॥
ततस्तु राजा सिन्धूनां वार्धक्षत्रिर्महायशाः। विवाहकामः शाल्वेयान् प्रयातः सोऽभवत् तदा॥६॥
verses.english: At that time the illustrious king of Sindhu, the son of Vriddhakshatra was, for marriage, going to the territory of Shalva,

verses.sanskrit: महता परिबर्हेण राजयोग्येन संवृतः। राजभिर्बहुभिः सार्धमुपायात् काम्यकं च सः॥७॥
verses.english: Dressed in his best royal robe and accompanied by many princes he halted at the forest of Kamayaka.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रापश्यत् प्रियां भार्यां पाण्डवानां यशस्विनीम्। तिष्ठन्तीमाश्रमद्वारि द्रौपदीं निर्जने वने॥८॥
verses.english: In that solitary place he found the handsome Draupadi, the beloved and the illustrious wife of the Pandavas, standing at the threshold of the hermitage.
verses.bhavadeepa: परिबर्हेण परिच्छदेन ‘परिबर्हं तु राजार्हवस्तुन्यपि परिच्छदे’ इति विश्वः ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजमानां वपुषा बिभ्रतीं रूपमुत्तमम्। भ्राजयन्तीं वनोद्देशं नीलाभ्रमिव विद्युतम्॥९॥
verses.english: She appeared in her form having the most excellent beauty, shedding lustre on woodland like lightning illuminating masses of dark clouds.

verses.sanskrit: अप्सरा देवकन्या वा माया वा देवनिर्मिता। इति कृत्वाऽञ्जलिं सर्वे ददृशुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥१०॥
verses.english: (Thinking): “Is she an Apsara or the daughter of a god or a celestials phantom,” they all with joined hands, stood gazing on the perfect and faultless beauty of her person.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स राजा सिन्धूनां वार्धक्षत्रिर्जयद्रथः। विस्मितस्त्वनवद्याङ्गीं दृष्ट्वा तां दुष्टमानसः॥११॥
verses.english: Seeing that lady of faultless feature, Jayadratha, the king of Sindhu, the son of Vriddhakshatra, possessed by evil intention.

verses.sanskrit: स कोटिकास्यं राजानमब्रवीत् काममोहितः। कस्य त्वेषाऽनवद्याङ्गी यदि वाऽपि न मानुषी॥१२॥
verses.english: Possessed by desire he said to the prince named Kotikasya, “Who is this lady of faultless feature? Is she a human being?

verses.sanskrit: विवाहार्थो न मे कश्चिदिमां प्राप्यातिसुन्दरीम्। एतामेवाहमादाय गमिष्यामि स्वमालयम्॥१३॥
verses.english: I do not desire to marry if I can secure this exquisitely beautiful lady. Taking her with me I shall go back to my house.
verses.bhavadeepa: कोटिकास्यं कोटी दुर्गमन्तःपुरं तत्राधिकृताः कोटिकाः तेषाम् आस्यमिव मुख्यम् । आख्यमिति पाठे सङ्ख्यान्तरं वक्तारमिति वा । अश्येति पाठे कोटिकाः अश्याः व्याप्या यस्येति वा राजानं क्षत्रियं प्रभुं वा । ‘राजा प्रभौ च नृपतौ क्षत्रिये रजनीपतौ’ इति मेदिनी ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: यच्छ जानीहि सौम्येमां कस्य वाऽत्र कुतोऽपि वा। किमर्थमागता सुभ्रूरिदं कण्टकितं वनम्॥१४॥
verses.english: O gentle sir, go and enquire who she is and whence she has come and why she, of fine eyebrows, has come to this forest full of thorns.

verses.sanskrit: अपि नाम वरारोहा मामेषा लोकसुन्दरी। भजेदद्यायतापाङ्गी सुदती तनुमध्यमा॥१५॥
verses.english: was Will this most excellent beauty of the world, this slender-waisted lady, having beautiful teeth and large eyes, accept me as her lord?

verses.sanskrit: अप्यहं कृतकामः स्यामिमां प्राप्य वरस्त्रियम्। गच्छ जानीहि को न्वस्या नाथ इत्येव कोटिक॥१६॥
verses.english: I shall certainly consider myself successful if I can obtain this best of females. Go Kotika and learn who her husband is.” Hearing this Kotikasya, wearing a Kundala, jumped out of the car and approached her as a jackal comes near a tigress and spoke to her.

verses.sanskrit: स कोटिकास्यस्तच्छ्रुत्वा रथात् प्रस्कन्द्य कुण्डली। उपेत्य पप्रच्छ तदा क्रोष्टा व्याघ्रवधूमिव॥१७॥
